grounding.quote: This profile is operational and stands on its own.

concepts.label: Design-module profile
concepts.definition: An operational engineering profile for preferred realisation structure and design discipline. Its engineering Ontology concerns one designed boundary; using the profile does not require adopting a world-model, Constraint-Emergence Ontology, or metaphysical or empirical programme.

grounding.quote:
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings.

concepts.label: Computational realisation projection
concepts.definition: The three domain views show domain structure, execution and lifecycle. A computational realisation projection additionally exposes abstract data types, identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings, including repeated machinery obscured by domain names.

grounding.quote: A component's declared role set is design authority;

concepts.label: Component role set
concepts.definition: The explicit semantic and operational roles declared for a material realisation component. The declared role set is design authority; technological capability creates no authority.

grounding.quote:
It treats a Markov object
as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose
effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is
load-bearing for context.

concepts.label: Markov-object theoretical framing
concepts.definition: Optional theoretical framing in which a Markov object is a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern with an effective blanket separating identity-bearing from contextual structure. IACS analogises the smallest such cut; the Promotion Test asks whether a payload has independent boundary authority; Boundary Inflation mistakes fragments for peer objects; semantic-boundary strong typing keeps the cut explicit.

grounding.quote:
- constructor or materialisation module: writes generated or built
  artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans.

concepts.label: Module role taxonomy
concepts.definition: Recommended module roles: carrier modules define typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells perform emission, publication, network, subprocess, persistence or delivery effects; projections derive read models or reports from authoritative truth; bindings/adapters translate external boundaries to internal carriers without inventing law; constructors/materialisers write generated or built artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Module boundaries constrain traversal reasoning under finite context, attention and time, expose ownership, consumption, emissions and sufficient proof, and make recurrence visible for library consolidation.
conditions: The profile governs the realisation boundary.

concepts.label: Typed truth carrier
concepts.definition: Typed values carrying source truth, preferably produced by a constructor or parser, consumed by transforms that return another carrier or closed result, and read by projections without mutation.

grounding.quote:
The outcome values a
semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

concepts.label: Semantic function and Product outcomes
concepts.definition: A Product semantic function may encounter input outside its admitted domain. Its returned outcomes are Product domain values, distinct from the method's core results; an evaluation consuming those outcomes returns its own core result.

grounding.quote:
Typical effect edges include file writes, network calls, subprocess
execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and
database mutation.

concepts.label: Effect edge
concepts.definition: An explicit boundary for effects such as file writes, network calls, subprocess execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation.

grounding.quote:
A
module is acting as an unlawful semantic centre when reviewers have to
read it to discover what counts as closure, what identity means, what
failure means, what work is next, or what the current truth is.

concepts.label: Hidden semantic centre
concepts.definition: A hidden semantic centre is an orchestration or wrapper surface that procedurally holds meaning which should already reside in carriers, contracts or explicit design modules. Its diagnostic is needing to read that module to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth.

grounding.quote:
Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary
and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor
should do the work.

concepts.label: Governance and strategy surfaces
concepts.definition: A boundary governing, observing, routing, auditing or evaluating another actor, executor, builder or substrate. Governance surfaces describe facts, state, boundary and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should work.

grounding.quote:
This does not
outrank constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence or
functional equivalence; it is subordinate to them.

concepts.label: Opportunistic optimisation
concepts.definition: Opportunistic optimisation is local improvement subordinate to constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Cross-boundary improvements are repricing inputs rather than silently enlarged clean-up.
conditions: A realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation work.

grounding.quote:
When the same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed
boundary, review treats that pattern as a commonisation candidate rather
than as another purely local clean-up

concepts.label: Recurrence extraction and commonisation
concepts.definition: Review of repeated realisation machinery as a commonisation candidate. Typical candidates are authority-neutral, not Product truth, reused across two or more tickets or boundaries, and locally adaptable without changing semantic ownership: expectation derivation, nested contract or policy carriers, proof helpers, fixtures, effect plans and constructors that own no semantic law.

grounding.quote:
The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction.

concepts.label: Post-ticket bounded design check
concepts.definition: A bounded design check against the accepted design basis and exact closure claim. Its complete selected function is the claim's causal closure, not the whole Product or construction history; it reconstructs governing requirements through Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, target modules, implementation and module-owned proof.
conditions: A ticket applies the profile to a boundary and claims that boundary has been processed.

concepts.label: Interface family and semantic bleed
concepts.definition: An interface family has one authoritative source truth consumed downstream. Interface bleed includes reconstructing another family's truth, projection becoming closure, reports/prompts becoming admission, wrappers deciding kernel semantics, or adapters inventing meaning.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
proofs to stay green while the old law still governs.

concepts.label: Proxy interface and retained compatibility
concepts.definition: A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that forwards to old authority, reconstructs missing truth from it, keeps it executable under a new name, or leaves proofs green while old law governs. Such substitution is bridge debt, distinct from explicitly retained compatibility.

grounding.quote:
A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour

When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks

concepts.label: Design review and functional checklist
concepts.definition: Review under the design profile includes provenance-bearing prompts, design-review questions, and an explicit functional-realisation checklist when functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low coupling is claimed.

grounding.quote:
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter.

concepts.label: Product adoption of the profile
concepts.definition: Product authority's adoption of an available design profile for a named boundary and, for partial adoption, a named rule family. Inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available but does not adopt it or create another adopter.

grounding.quote:
the UX profile ([UX](UX.md)) refines this profile for UX
surfaces with rendering, state-transition and effect-membrane rules and is
loaded only when the work realises a UX surface

concepts.label: Responsibilities of related members
concepts.definition: The source's allocation of member responsibilities: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and migration; RELEASE owns release cut, Product, install, qualification and version-line promotion evaluation; ODD owns graph-native constructive carrier law; DESIGN_MODULE owns preferred implementation/design module structure; UX adds rendering, state-transition, effect-membrane and AssetSurface-binding discipline for UX surfaces. ASSURANCE module lifecycle confirmation detects sufficient lifecycle signal for building and review, not release or rollout eligibility.

grounding.quote:
the permission is scoped to that role
and does not extend to other runtime realisations

concepts.label: Role-scoped runtime identity defaults
concepts.definition: A bound ABG runtime realisation may publish default identity generators, validators and normalisers for its own runtime surfaces and default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers.
conditions: A runtime realisation is consumer-bound to the ABG role under the graph-execution profile.

grounding.quote:
[Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) own the core result values this member
uses; it defines no result values of its own.

concepts.label: EVALUATION member
concepts.definition: A Tier 1 member owning justification and acceptance of claims, evidence, independent assessment, review results, acceptance, realisation conformance and the equivalence ladder, frame and method qualification, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention. It consumes FOUNDATIONS' core results and defines no result values itself.

grounding.quote:
A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.

concepts.label: Load-bearing claim
concepts.definition: A load-bearing assertion over an exact subject, property and governing basis, with a declared witness relation, excluded nearest weaker property and falsifier. Construction claims about recursive or repeated work distinguish preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work
this family governs, not commitments, and do not follow from finite
capacity alone.
P5 (derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise)
P4b (derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable)

concepts.label: Foundation-to-law family F6
concepts.definition: F6 is the claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance family covering EVALUATION §§1–5. Its instance premises are conditions of governed work, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. Its table traces consequences, rule owners, added policy/domain choices and consumers. P1, P2, P3 and P6 are cited as independent; P0 is recovered with named candidate-output or non-reacquirable-fact premises; P5 is derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise, and P4b from P0 and P2 with the step-produced-fact premise.
conditions: Exact-subject claims are relied on for promotion, closure or release.
Evidence is finite and may observe a weaker subject, another subject or another basis.
A constructor may be probabilistic or otherwise fallible.
Each reliance boundary has a decision owner.

concepts.label: Bases, roles and structural/semantic separation
concepts.definition: Three distinct bases: semantic basis comprises constitutional and accepted-design relations defining claim meaning; evidence basis comprises exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations; state projection is a current view derived from admitted semantic and evidence bases. Four distinct roles define law, supply observations, apply the declared evaluation relation and dispose by decision authority. Structural conformance concerns closed syntax, types, identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates; semantic fidelity concerns meaning and materiality.

grounding.quote:
Authorship is one of the conditions on
which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
the other

concepts.label: Independent assessment
concepts.definition: Assessment independent in authorship and evidence conditions. Constructor self-review remains construction output. Author identity is the party responsible for realised content; actor identity identifies whoever performs an operation and is not authority. Independence is not established by a fresh context or assumed across actor families.

grounding.quote:
A declared predicate the review planned and did
not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses

concepts.label: Review result and absence of evaluation
concepts.definition: A review returns one FOUNDATIONS core result per declared predicate actually evaluated, accompanied by exact subject and basis, consulted evidence, consequence-ranked findings with evidence and smallest bounded correction, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. A planned but unperformed predicate has no result, unlike an evaluated undecided predicate or required coverage with no planned assessment.

grounding.quote:
The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states

concepts.label: Technical triage projection
concepts.definition: Finding-level, evidence-bound assessment against the exact evaluated claim and basis. Severity is the assessor's consequence grade; priority, current promotion-boundary effect and disposition belong to the decision owner. Triage payload classes complete, indeterminate and not_applicable are neither core results nor dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states.
conditions: A review returns findings with technical triage.

concepts.label: Acceptance and work-item closure
concepts.definition: Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject, bounded to its named instance and interval. Work-item closure is satisfaction of the item's stated closing condition; review is an input rather than closure.

grounding.quote:
This section is the
one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
refer to it and add only their domain triggers.

concepts.label: Finding-dependent promotion blocking
concepts.definition: A finding is a reported defect against the exact evaluated claim. Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act over that finding. EVALUATION §5 supplies the shared blocking conditions; profiles and work carriers add only domain triggers.

grounding.quote:
A realisation aⱼ conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour
satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract (P1) and an independent
judgment (P6). Several realisations may conform to one Σ; sufficiency does
not require unique derivation or equality with an incumbent.

concepts.label: Realisation conformance
concepts.definition: A realisation conforms to specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Several realisations may conform; sufficiency does not require unique derivation or incumbent equality.

grounding.quote:
the rungs are listed, not ordered, and no rung implies
another. Conformance, semantic equivalence, computational equivalence and
categorical equivalence are separate claims with separate evidence

concepts.label: Unordered equivalence ladder
concepts.definition: Four listed, unordered, mutually non-implying claim kinds: conformance; semantic equivalence of realisations, meaning identical interpreted behaviour on a stated domain including behaviour outside Σ; computational equivalence, meaning the same function at equal cost for declared workloads on architecture H; and categorical equivalence of categories and maps. Semantic equivalence here is not cross-context concept equivalence. Preservation of identities and composition by a map is a further distinct claim.

grounding.quote:
A specification arranged in layers is sufficient when
a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer; the
derivation need not be unique, since different realisations may satisfy the
same upper layer, and the test is sufficiency, not determinism.

concepts.label: Layered sufficiency and reconstruction
concepts.definition: A layered specification is sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from every layer. The test is sufficiency, not unique derivation or determinism; reconstructability requires a correct route, not executing it on every use.

grounding.quote:
Demonstrated
reduction: a deciding path of the successor costs less than the same path
in the predecessor on a declared measure, shown by the trace of both paths
with the declared tradeoffs. Mere relocation: text moved from one owner or
carrier to another without a change in meaning and without a traced
change in any deciding path.

concepts.label: Three-part reconstruction return
concepts.definition: A reconstruction return separates semantic conservation, demonstrated reduction and mere relocation. Conservation preserves the meaning of a disposed predecessor claim, judged by reading both texts against the disposition. Reduction shows lower cost for the same deciding path on a declared measure through traces of both paths and declared tradeoffs. Relocation moves text between owners or carriers without changed meaning or a traced deciding-path change.
conditions: A task builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor.

grounding.quote:
computational similarity
  -> commonisation candidate
  -> semantic and operational equivalence evaluation
  -> reuse, parameterised common relation, or justified separation

relations.meaning: The computational projection exposes commonisation candidates for semantic and operational evaluation; discovery does not itself decide reuse or separation.
conditions: Computational similarity is discovered.
exceptions: Similarity does not establish semantic equivalence or authority.

grounding.quote:
The framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the
scope of the profile

relations.meaning: The Markov-object analogy explains the engineering profile without governing its use or adding prerequisites.
exceptions: The framing may be irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class.

grounding.quote:
Whether
a finding also blocks the boundary's current promotion is decided by
[EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion).

relations.meaning: The shared promotion-blocking law determines the current-promotion effects of the design check; the design profile contributes domain triggers only.
conditions: A design-check finding is considered for current promotion.

grounding.quote:
When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the
named boundary

relations.meaning: Product adoption determines the named boundary over which the profile is consistently applied; availability alone does not activate it.
conditions: Product authority adopts the profile.
exceptions: Explicit partial adoption may narrow the boundary and rule-family scope.

grounding.quote:
which is
evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one.

relations.meaning: A review recommendation supplies evidence to the decision owner; it neither applies a disposition nor constitutes acceptance or closure.
conditions: A review recommends a disposition.

grounding.quote:
The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload

relations.meaning: A review's core result determines the described triage-payload class and consumption restrictions; the payload is distinct from the result and decision.
conditions: A finding-level triage is returned for an evaluated predicate.
exceptions: An unperformed predicate has no result or triage payload.

grounding.quote:
The three heads stay separate in the return as the rungs of the
ladder do above; a frame for a reconstruction task binds this
distinction.

relations.meaning: The return's three independent evidence heads preserve the same separation principle illustrated by the ladder; this analogy establishes no implication between claims.
conditions: A reconstruction return makes conservation, reduction or relocation claims.

grounding.quote:
Use of a
component outside its declared role set does not silently establish
identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth

constraints.statement: Every material component declares its semantic and operational role set. Where a role bears authority, composition and use preserve its applicable IDENTITY §6 authority relation; that section supports rather than owns the role model. New operational responsibility and new semantic or authoritative roles are design changes requiring re-entry; behaviour already within an abstract declared role is ordinary variation. Out-of-role use establishes none of identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced authority relation is not fully supplied.
conditions: A material realisation component is composed or used.

grounding.quote:
Component-local success cannot establish the complete-path
claim, and different names do not establish different computational
responsibilities

constraints.statement: Project the domain into its computational realisation and extend cross-view evaluation to prove they describe one system. Identify fact establishment, consuming operations, applicable basis and invalidators, effect boundaries, retained alternatives and accumulated work using ACTIVATION §§4 and 7; include method and assurance operations where material. Declare supported input dimensions, workload, growth and assumptions needed for the selected outcome; distinguish material startup, framework, external-computation, transport and assurance costs under ACTIVATION §6. Bind any acceptance limits and owner before qualification, challenge assumptions on representative supported paths and material growth, and observe work directly when elapsed time cannot locate it without repeating operations merely to count them. Existing design/proof surfaces suffice; no additional accounting system or fixed complexity is required. Local success and differing names cannot establish whole-path success or different computational responsibilities.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced enclosing-relation, reuse and cost laws are not fully supplied.
conditions: At a material semantic boundary.
For material producer-to-consumer paths and material algorithmic work.

grounding.quote:
A materially non-equivalent law among
those dimensions requires separation. Other differences justify separation
only when evaluation shows that parameterisation or adaptation would
weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational
constraints.

or a local realisation presents an existing accepted
relation as newly owned local truth.

constraints.statement: The subordinate projection cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority. Similarity yields a commonisation candidate, followed by semantic and operational equivalence evaluation, then reuse, a parameterised common relation or justified separation. Material non-equivalence in identity/key law, ownership, ordering, admissible mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure, access policy, lifecycle or authority over truth requires separation; other differences justify it only if parameterisation/adaptation would weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints. A difference alone does not discharge Prime contraction or recurrence review. Each material obligation in M(B) has both a semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, new candidate relation) and realisation disposition (consume, implement locally, optimise, adapt, deliberately duplicate under stated non-semantic constraints). The law is falsified by materially equivalent domain-named implementations without semantic disposition, generic machinery becoming semantic authority, superficial commonisation despite incompatible identity/ordering/failure/ownership/lifecycle law, or local realisation presenting accepted relations as newly owned truth.
constraints.uncertainty: M(B) and the full Prime law are referenced but not defined in the supplied section.
conditions: Computational similarity or a material algorithmic obligation in M(B) is present.

grounding.quote:
This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite. The rules
of this profile remain engineering law even where the Markov-object
construct is irrelevant, unavailable or still only candidate-class

constraints.statement: The framing is optional theoretical justification, adds no prerequisite and expands no profile scope. The source's engineering rules remain applicable even when the Markov-object construct is irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class.
constraints.uncertainty: No empirical or metaphysical validity of the framing is asserted.

grounding.quote:
modules should be
classified by role (P0, P6). Recommended
roles are:

for a boundary this
profile governs they read through the binding declared at the head of this
member

constraints.statement: Modules should be classified by role; the listed roles are recommendations. Design-to-module evidence, module-derived unit tests and module lifecycle confirmation remain ASSURANCE §§14–16 law, read through the member-head binding for a governed boundary.
constraints.uncertainty: ASSURANCE §§14–16 and the member-head binding are outside the supplied source.
conditions: This profile governs a realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
Projects using this profile prefer one algebraic primitive plus
projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total
functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds

constraints.statement: Prefer one algebraic primitive with projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds.
constraints.uncertainty: These are preferences, not unconditional prohibitions of every alternative.
conditions: A project uses the profile.

grounding.quote:
Mutable
carrier state requires explicit justification when it is
performance-critical, required by the host runtime or framework, or
modelling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth.
Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values. Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification for performance-critical use, host runtime/framework requirements, or modelling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth. Convenience is insufficient.
constraints.uncertainty: The general preference is distinguished from the stricter functional-claim checklist.
conditions: Values carry source truth.
exceptions: Mutation is materially necessary.

grounding.quote:
Semantic functions should be total or as close to total as the language
and problem allow

They should avoid partial
functions that assume hidden preconditions, semantic `.get(...)` fallback
chains, and controller code that reconstructs missing truth from defaults

constraints.statement: Prefer totality, boundary rejection of invalid input, admitted carriers in semantic kernels, typed explicit failure, Result-like or closed outcome carriers, explicit validation and unsupported/rejected outcomes. Avoid hidden-precondition partial functions, semantic fallback chains and controller reconstruction from defaults. Product outcome values must remain distinct from method evaluation results.
constraints.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS' full result algebra is not supplied.
conditions: A semantic function is realised under the profile.
exceptions: Totality is bounded by what the language and problem allow.
Typed explicit failure is preferred when practical.

grounding.quote:
If a function both decides the
semantic meaning and directly performs the write, the design should be
treated as suspect.

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit and isolated; kernels should not perform effects while deciding law. Prefer the ordered sequence: admit/parse authoritative input, transform to typed plan/outcome, apply edge effects from it, publish resulting events/projections downstream. A function deciding meaning and directly writing should be treated as suspect.
constraints.uncertainty: This paragraph states a preference and diagnostic, not an executed sequence.

grounding.quote:
No controller, manager, service method, runtime loop or public wrapper
should be the hidden semantic centre of the system

constraints.statement: Controllers, managers, service methods, runtime loops and public wrappers should not hide semantic meaning through procedural decisions, payload-fragment reconstruction, legacy/fallback rehydration, or ad hoc dictionaries and .get chains. Closure, identity, failure, next work and current truth should already be explicit in carriers, contracts or design modules.

grounding.quote:
Reducing coupling
means reducing the number of places where meaning can be invented.

constraints.statement: Reduce coupling by dependency shape, not file count alone. The preferred displayed direction is carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections, rather than controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections. Excess coupling includes many modules reading/mutating one object, projections inferring truth from implementation state, consumers silently rebuilding source truth from raw artifacts, or tests passing only because multiple modules duplicate meaning. Reduction means fewer places where meaning can be invented.
constraints.uncertainty: The arrow is retained as the source's preferred dependency direction, without inferring execution or authority from it.

grounding.quote:
it publishes governance truth, not
imperative strategy law, unless strategy ownership is explicitly part of
the boundary's ratified responsibility

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth: current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure/unresolved identities, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and prior-turn/run continuity. Do not drift into replacement decision-engine behaviour through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers. Imperative repair instructions, framework preferences disguised as observability, budgets/scores/counters/ratings recreating another actor's judgment, and hidden doctrine in prompts/reports/read models are unlawful absent the applicable explicit ownership exception.
conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
exceptions: Imperative strategy is permitted when strategy ownership is explicitly part of the boundary's ratified responsibility.
Assessment that reproduces another actor's judgment requires explicit ownership of that assessment boundary.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic
optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design
or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;
authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;
visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and
effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or
bootstrap doctrine.

constraints.statement: The opened area should be improved, subject to constitutional truth, ownership evidence and equivalence. Lawful optimisation must be boundary-local, behaviour-preserving, authority-neutral, visibility-neutral and effect-neutral. Removing local parser re-entry, consolidating local routes, improving a local algorithm/scan, or simplifying proof fixtures/tests without changing module claims can qualify. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing, changed public carriers/visibility/truth ownership, wider effects or observability doctrine, and performance changes to Product expectations require explicit design re-entry. Cross-boundary discoveries remain repricing inputs; admitted follow-up enters separately at the smallest lawful re-entry point. TICKETS, not this scope rule, owns follow-up recording and ticket closure effects.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD §4 and TICKETS mechanics are not supplied.
conditions: A boundary is lawfully open for bounded work.

grounding.quote:
a third local rebuild
is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an
existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface
before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit
do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific

shared names, fewer lines or
an unused common helper do not establish contraction

constraints.statement: Treat recurrence as a commonisation candidate. TICKETS §6 owns the rule of two, third-rebuild threshold, commonisation order and library_usage/governing_library/library_rationale fields for every implementation migration ticket. For design conformance a third rebuild must consume a reusable surface, extend it before local implementation lands, or record the stated exception. Tenant-local authority-neutral reusable patterns should be extracted. Changes to ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or shared common law are separate design decisions. Commonisation closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and superseded production responsibility is retired or satisfies SPEC_METHOD §7 retention. Compare removed work and maintained responsibilities across the path; names, line count and unused helpers prove no contraction.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete ticket commonisation order and retention relation are not supplied.
conditions: A pattern recurs across more than one processed boundary.
The third-local-rebuild condition applies when such a rebuild is proposed.
exceptions: A third rebuild may remain boundary-specific when review explicitly records a do-not-commonise decision and rationale.

grounding.quote:
whether any discovered
issue falsifies the current claim or an applicable hard stop

No processed ticket that applies this profile should claim
design-method closure until this bounded design check is complete.

constraints.statement: Check the accepted design basis and exact closure claim before claiming closure; implementation status alone is insufficient. Determine lawfulness under current design/module assets, inclusion of every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained predecessor claim, competing/ambiguous acceptance-path authority, durable architectural foreclosure of an admitted Product outcome, and falsification of the claim or an applicable hard stop. Reconstruct the complete selected function rather than only revisiting previous findings. Hashes establish identity; headings/artifact presence establish location; tests establish only asserted properties. None supplies missing semantic relations or permits substitution of weaker claims. TICKETS retains status, closure, reopening, dependency and follow-up mechanics.
conditions: A processed ticket applies the profile and claims design-method closure.
exceptions: The check may be part of normal verification; no separate artifact, round or reviewer is required.

grounding.quote:
Missing, stale or ambiguous coverage is not a
no-delta proof. A material changed relation or a new counterexample is an
instance of that section's material input change: it requires affected
reconstruction and the applicable design gate, conserving supported
unaffected relations.

constraints.statement: Confirm exact scope, traces, applicability and absence of ACTIVATION §7 invalidators before reuse. The source states that §7 owns exactly three invalidators and no fourth. Governing-source repricing is changed basis invalidating only affected Ontology relations and downstream projections pending impact evaluation. A later applicable candidate that could materially alter the lawful frontier changes affected selection inputs; evidence or a material dimension defeating dominance changes that relation's inputs. A new role, conversation or review occurrence alone does not require evidence re-authoring or recreating views. Missing/stale/ambiguous coverage is no no-delta proof. Material relation changes and new counterexamples require affected reconstruction and the applicable gate while conserving supported unaffected relations.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete enumeration of ACTIVATION §7's three invalidators is not present; the supplied examples identify changed basis and material input change only.
conditions: Reuse of current accepted Ontology, design verdict or sufficient reconstruction evidence is proposed for an unchanged boundary.
exceptions: New or materially changed boundaries still require complete Ontology and three-view coverage.

grounding.quote:
an issue that falsifies the current claim or an
applicable hard stop blocks the design-method closure claim, because that
claim is then `falsified`, which never becomes `satisfied`

repricing inputs that do not automatically widen the subject, block its
bounded claim or require a follow-up ticket

constraints.statement: A falsified current claim or applicable hard stop blocks design-method closure; falsified does not become satisfied and a hard stop is not waived. Current-promotion effects use EVALUATION §5: falsifying issue, competing/ambiguous authority, unlawful current boundary or omitted applicable requirement/design/predecessor claim, and durable architectural foreclosure supply its four domain triggers. Wording cannot narrow away active applicable authority. Absorb local clean-up/commonisation only when needed to make the claim true, preserve singular authority, satisfy accepted design or avoid foreclosure. Other clean-up, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary opportunities remain out-of-claim repricing inputs; they do not automatically widen scope, block the bounded claim or require follow-up. Owner-admitted repricing enters at the smallest lawful re-entry point; unclaimed future capability and optional clean-up are not implicit work.
conditions: The bounded design check discovers an issue or opportunity.

grounding.quote:
Low
coupling requires semantic non-bleed, not only small functions.

constraints.statement: No interface should bleed semantic authority into another family. Each family requires one authoritative source truth, downstream consumption of that truth and no new semantic centre created by crossing the interface boundary. Low coupling requires semantic non-bleed as well as small functions.

grounding.quote:
If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof; otherwise
the proxy path is removed.

constraints.statement: Proxy or partial interfaces do not substitute for real migration or design completion. Absent explicitly bounded and proved compatibility, remove the proxy path.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD §7's fuller bridge prohibition is not supplied.
conditions: A project uses this profile.
exceptions: Intentionally retained compatibility is an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof.

grounding.quote:
A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour

constraints.statement: Profile prompts follow ACTIVATION §2 prompt construction. Design-enforcing clauses need provenance and proof of continuing intended causal or preventive effect.
constraints.uncertainty: The external prompt-construction rule is not supplied.
conditions: A prompt under the profile contains a clause intended to enforce design law.

grounding.quote:
Would removing the authoritative carrier make the system fail closed
   rather than silently rebuilding truth?

If the ticket is making a design-method closure claim, did the bounded
    design check cover the exact claim and applicable hard stops without
    automatically absorbing optional discovery?

constraints.statement: Ask whether law resides in carriers rather than orchestration; steps transform admitted truth; effects are isolated; projections/reports cannot invent closure or same-name structurally different truth; mutation is justified, bounded and local; consumers can directly pattern-match carriers; proxies are not silently authoritative; removal of authority fails closed; new functions project accepted Prime atoms without convenience aggregation or rival authority; interfaces do not bleed; Python avoids Any/open dictionaries/untyped semantic definitions; IACS is declared; subordinate payloads remain justified as subordinate; promoted types pass the Promotion Test; typed closure avoids Boundary Inflation and parallel schema migrations; truth surfaces do not increase and duplicate truth is reduced; foreign/open payloads are not trusted past ingress; enforcement follows proof. Also ask whether governance publishes state/routes rather than strategy; reference design explicitly derives target design then module assets; module-domain projections faithfully show IACS, Prime mappings, payloads, visibility, ownership and deferred families; tests derive from ownership/assets; optimisation remains local, behaviour-preserving and authority-neutral; cross-boundary opportunities require owner-admitted re-entry; recurrence receives an explicit commonisation decision and third rebuild consumes/extends or records do-not-commonise; closure checks exact claims and hard stops without automatic optional work.
constraints.uncertainty: These are required review questions, not assertions that the reviewed properties hold.
conditions: Reviewing code under this profile.
exceptions: Python-specific checks apply to governed Python surfaces.
Reference-to-target derivation checks apply when a reference realisation exists.
Governance, optimisation, recurrence and ticket checks apply when their stated circumstances occur.

grounding.quote:
Does every rejected material candidate carry decisive evidence or a
    falsifier, while an unresolved frontier remains a gap rather than an
    unsupported preference?

constraints.statement: Ask whether capability was stated without Product/domain/module/vendor/file/incumbent labels, separating declared semantic/authority relations from generic mechanics; bounded discovery records every searched source/category, cutoff time, version basis, applicability, exclusions, predecessor/incumbent status and residual unknown; later material candidates invalidate affected evidence; credible compositions are compared across decision-relevant lifecycle dimensions without incumbent/source-order/local-code/dependency-count preference; hard authority, Product-contract, safety, security, licensing and constructability failures eliminate candidates while unknowns stay explicit; reused foundations hold only assigned roles preserving owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle and refusal invariants; selected composition is undominated and the existing trade-off owner applies declared priorities/risk tolerances without inventing total ordering; every rejected material candidate has decisive evidence or a falsifier and unresolved frontiers remain gaps; newly exposed material generic subproblems recursively re-enter selection before implementation is retained.
constraints.uncertainty: The full UP-023 selection relation is outside this source segment.
conditions: Reviewing construction or selection of a material generic capability or common mechanic.

grounding.quote:
A missing authority declaration or observation does not by itself show
excessive coupling or imperative design. That diagnosis requires evidence
that meaning is held in orchestration or outside the declared carriers
and transforms

constraints.statement: Withhold the dependent conformance claim, record the unanswered relation and deciding evidence needed, and diagnose the gap at its actual owner under ACTIVATION §1. Missing authority declarations or observations alone do not prove excessive coupling or imperative design; those diagnoses require evidence of meaning in orchestration or outside declared carriers/transforms.
constraints.uncertainty: An unanswered relation remains unresolved, not falsified by absence.
conditions: A required relation is unanswered.

grounding.quote:
a negative proof shows that an imperative bypass, open-payload
      bypass or effect-edge erasure fails closed;

constraints.statement: Explicitly check: constitutional WHAT is preserved within lawful HOW; one accepted Ontology derives entities, identities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle, authority, atomic functions, composition, effects and projections; every create/read/update/delete lifecycle question has a lawful function, reasoned not_applicable or owned gap; authority kinds are distinct; every functionality item is disposed without direct verb promotion; whole-family Prime contraction precedes peer promotion and records all atom domains/projection maps; IACS/views/contracts/adapters/code/tests are fidelity-checked Ontology projections. Check reference-boundary equivalence and design-to-design-to-module mapping before implementation where applicable, and proportional generic-foundation selection with discovery/frontier/roles/evidence. Implementation and tests derive from the same module assets; each truth surface has one owner; duplicate truth/reconstruction/rival paths decrease; functions consume admitted carriers and are pure for equal inputs; time/randomness/UUIDs/environment/process/filesystem/network/registries and shared mutable state are absent from the semantic centre; identity creation is ingress/effect-owned; carriers return new immutable values; local admitted truth does not re-enter parsers/validators/loaders; ingress rejects incomplete/invalid truth; defaults are ratified and carrier-owned; each function has one owner/responsibility. Algebra depends on carrier contracts, admission on validation, effects stay typed at edges without erasing truth into open objects; no function both decides meaning and performs effects; package/bootstrap/controller/adapter/runtime layers stay below the semantic centre; governance publishes facts, eligibility and provenance only. Require matching complete Mermaid views, complete cross-view matrix and explicit accepted verdict without bypassed gaps; module-owned tests; lawful local optimisation; explicit recurrence decisions, consumption/extension of available common surfaces or rationale for non-use; owner-admitted cross-boundary re-entry; bounded closure checks; negative fail-closed proof for imperative/open-payload/effect-erasure bypasses; graph-governed modules inside declared traversals and repricing when modules decide next work, closure, semantic target movement or graph identity; lifecycle confirmation with answers, reasoned non-applicability or named gaps and authority-grounded operational claims.
constraints.uncertainty: Checklist claims are represented as review obligations, not verified properties of any Product.
conditions: A project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation.
exceptions: Reference equivalence and explicit reference-to-target derivation apply when a reference exists.
Identity creation ownership applies when identity is introduced.
Optimisation, recurrence, cross-boundary, ticket and graph checks apply when their stated triggers occur.

grounding.quote:
accepted Ontology before promotion or closure and, where
      design-gated, before retained implementation establishes an
      unresolved or contradictory relation or chooses a materially
      non-equivalent network;

For an unchanged boundary, the hard gate is the accepted basis plus
evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not require a new
Ontology, IACS, three-view asset, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane

constraints.statement: The language-agnostic gate covers module, carrier, data-entity and realisation review. Require accepted Ontology before promotion/closure and, where design-gated, before retained implementation establishes unresolved/contradictory relations or materially non-equivalent networks; complete lifecycle/authority/function derivation; whole-family Prime, admitted domains, projection mappings and composition/effect algebra; proportional capability/foundation selection for material generic mechanics/dependencies with bounded discovery, frontier disposition and exact role/authority conservation; pure semantic functions; immutable carriers without shared mutable semantic state; one owner per truth; low admission/algebra/effect coupling; no hidden runtime authority; accepted domain/sequence/state projections; complete cross-view evaluation without bypassed gaps; specification equivalence and reference equivalence when present; lifecycle confirmation or named gaps; and negative proof for imperative/open bypass.
constraints.uncertainty: Named lifecycle gaps are expressly retained by the gate; they are not silently converted to resolved phases.
conditions: The hard gate is applied to a new or materially changed boundary.
exceptions: For an unchanged boundary, use the accepted basis plus evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta; no new Ontology, IACS, views, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane is required.

grounding.quote:
For
migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance
boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)
explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit

When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming
closure for that change

constraints.statement: Apply adoption consistently across Ontology/architecture, design modules, runtime/execution kernels, prompts/reports, constructors/materialisers and projections/queries in the named boundary. Carrier/schema closure and governance migrations should state boundary closure evaluators explicitly in the governing ADR/ticket. Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares/cites accepted Ontology before completion, with change-proportionate lifecycle, authority, function derivation, whole-family Prime, atom domains, realisation maps and traceability. Schema/typed-carrier changes derive and reconcile IACS first; reference-derived changes publish reference-to-target derivation and Ontology-derived three views first; active implementation publishes a module-derived unit-test lane before closure. Partial adoption should explicitly name boundary and rule family.
constraints.uncertainty: Boundary closure evaluator details and ASSURANCE §15 are outside the supplied sections.
conditions: Product authority adopts the profile for a named boundary.
exceptions: Partial adoption may narrow scope but cannot omit evidence needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct a boundary while claiming completion.

grounding.quote:
For products governed by the graph-execution profile, that profile decides
whether the operative unit is an outcome traversal, graph function, GTL
module or ABG runtime boundary; this profile then governs the
deterministic module structure that realises, evaluates, adapts or
projects inside that boundary

constraints.statement: ODD decides the operative graph unit; DESIGN_MODULE governs deterministic realisation/evaluation/adaptation/projection inside it. Load UX only for UX realisation; its render purity, reducer purity, effect membrane and AssetSurface binding add functional front/back consistency. Module lifecycle confirmation detects adequate lifecycle signal for build/review but does not decide release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector promotion, installation policy or rollout; RELEASE and project-owned release/deployment/operational surfaces retain those decisions.
constraints.uncertainty: The other members' full operative laws are not supplied.
conditions: A Product is governed by the graph-execution profile.
UX additions apply when the boundary realises a UX/UI surface.

grounding.quote:
Their standing as
defaults and the identity law of their override, its preservation
conditions and its publication surface are
[IDENTITY §7](IDENTITY.md#7-default-formats-and-overrides).

constraints.statement: Default publication is confined to the bound role's own runtime surfaces and default ODD kinds used by default F_D helpers; it extends no permission to other runtime realisations. Default standing, override identity law, preservation conditions and publication surface belong to IDENTITY §7.
constraints.uncertainty: IDENTITY §7's override requirements are unresolved in this source selection.
conditions: The realisation is consumer-bound to the ABG role under graph execution.

grounding.quote:
the composition and effect algebra
that remains required where a boundary composes higher-order or effectful
computation are stated once in
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape](SPEC_METHOD.md#realisation-shape)

constraints.statement: The profile does not mandate one programming language, elimination of all imperative code, monadic/category-theory vocabulary or custom algebraic replacement of every exception. These non-goals do not remove the composition and effect algebra required for higher-order/effectful computation; SPEC_METHOD §2 owns the full realisation-shape rule.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete required algebra and implementation shape are not supplied.
conditions: A boundary composes higher-order or effectful computation.

grounding.quote:
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax,
compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a
semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because
the weaker property is easier to measure

constraints.statement: Before witness selection declare exact subject, property, basis, witness relation, excluded nearest weaker property and falsifier; otherwise the activity is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging/syntax/compilation/presence/invocation/local behaviour cannot substitute for semantic, authority, installed, release or end-to-end claims. Repeated/recursive construction claims state preservation, progress, termination or outcome satisfaction and whether the witness predicate is the full obligation, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction. Expected answers require assertion provenance and execution requires execution provenance; a passing necessary-condition check establishes only that condition.
constraints.uncertainty: The external provenance and construction relations are not fully supplied.
conditions: A load-bearing claim is made; additional construction-kind requirements apply to recursive or repeated work.

grounding.quote:
a planned or
specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,
and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim
remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property

constraints.statement: Checker/validator/harness/reviewer assurance binds the exact subject and authoritative composition relation. Single-file/carrier evidence proves only that boundary; cross-carrier satisfaction/conflict must be decided at the declared composite boundary. Mechanical-enforcement claims require a named executable/reproducible predicate and a witness reachable through the ordinary declared assurance path; until both are observed, the claim stays open or is explicitly downgraded to planned evidence.
constraints.uncertainty: No ordinary assurance path is instantiated by this interpretation.
conditions: Assurance supports promotion or closure.
Mechanical-enforcement requirements apply when mechanical enforcement is claimed.

grounding.quote:
A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated
evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared
inference relation, the relevant comparable population, explicit
counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence
invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is
superseded, withdrawn or requalified

constraints.statement: Quantifier, population and scope cannot outrun evaluated evidence. Generalisation needs a declared inference relation, comparable population, explicit counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence invalidates every dependent verdict until supersession, withdrawal or requalification of the claim-evidence relation. The source's boundary/quantifier rules are falsified by weaker/different-subject assurance, unevaluated composite closure from individual-carrier evidence, absent mechanical predicate/reachable witness, planned evidence reported as observed, unsupported generalisation, or dependent verdicts surviving material counterevidence without requalification.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not

constraints.statement: The table's consumers apply, without expanding, the owning rule. Claim-composition authority declares composite boundaries; project assurance design declares ordinary assurance paths; claim authors declare generalisation inference/population; models supply checker decision contracts. TICKETS policy identifies required independent-assessment boundaries and a governing basis may add them; governing authority configures actor type/count, rounds, engines, prompts and orchestration. This member owns assessor pre-exposure expectations, no repair, post-exposure intervention and same-family default non-independence. Adopting profiles declare triage fields; Products own scales, priority/boundary/cutoff policies. Governing bases name acceptance boundary, interval and owner; work items own closing conditions; humans admit bounded proxy grants; hard-stop owners and ACTIVATION §4 determine non-waivability; RELEASE owns successor dispositions and evaluation, while current Product authority owns removals. Core result algebra and planned-but-unevaluated absence remain FOUNDATIONS family F3, not new F6 result values.
constraints.uncertainty: The table identifies external owners and consumer loci; their full definitions are not imported.
conditions: A consumer applies an F6 rule.

grounding.quote:
A semantic change requires lawful re-entry and invalidates affected
downstream acceptance. A broad digest may conservatively
invalidate a review; it does not prove that every semantic relation
changed

constraints.statement: Keep semantic basis, evidence basis and state projection distinct, and separately record law, observations, evaluator application and decision disposition. RF-007 and AC-018 add only frame/model bindings. Evidence change may invalidate a verdict without changed law; ACTIVATION §7 decides when, and required invalidation occurs before reliance. Projection change may stale a view without changing truth under ACTIVATION §2. Semantic change requires lawful re-entry and invalidates affected downstream acceptance. Broad digest change may conservatively invalidate review but proves only representation change, not change to every semantic relation.
constraints.uncertainty: External reuse and staleness tests are not fully supplied.
exceptions: One actor may perform several roles if the record keeps them distinguishable.

grounding.quote:
Evidence bound to a basis other than
the evaluated one is excluded by basis; it is not admitted with a narrower
scope

constraints.statement: Structural success supplies evidence for semantic review and does not replace it. A checker decides the structural subset; semantic/authority claims require the stated contract. Valid parse, map, green test and historical judgment each establish only their own claim. Evidence on another basis is excluded, not admitted under a narrower scope; AC-018/AC-019 bind these distinctions to a_c records and validity.
constraints.uncertainty: The subject's referenced model laws are data and are not the selected calculus's operational application.
conditions: A checker or other evidence surface is used to support a claim.
exceptions: A checker may claim a semantic or authority subset under an exact lawful model-supplied decision contract.

grounding.quote:
The assessor records its
expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
own authorship.

constraints.statement: Assess exact live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not constructor summaries. For method qualification freeze identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere stabilise exact subject. Record expectations from governing source before opening candidate; read that fixed subject rather than a mutable tree; make no repairs and assess no own authorship. Post-exposure revision is a declared intervention, either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new qualification subject, and cannot retroactively pass the original frozen construction. This law prescribes no actor type/count, round count, engine, prompt or orchestration.
constraints.uncertainty: Required-assessment boundaries and method qualification's full protocol are not supplied.
conditions: Promotion requires independent assessment under TICKETS policy or an added governing-basis requirement.
exceptions: Shared mechanical evidence may be reused subject to ACTIVATION §7; the constructor's judgment may not.
Outside method qualification an equivalent exact-subject relation sufficient for the claim may replace immutable identity.

grounding.quote:
Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment

constraints.statement: Bind returned assessment to producer, subject, basis and evidence to authenticate it. Authentication establishes neither expected-answer assertion provenance nor run execution provenance; both remain separately required. Plan membership authenticates nothing. Unauthenticated results satisfy no required assessment and results bound to another subject satisfy no planned assessment.
constraints.uncertainty: The full FOUNDATIONS provenance and conjunction relations are not supplied.
conditions: An assessment is returned for required or planned assessment.
exceptions: No cryptographic or transport binding protocol is prescribed.

grounding.quote:
A person
who authored an adopted repair cannot supply its required independent
assessment by calling that authorship a finding

the default where it is not
stated is that they are not independent.

constraints.statement: Reporting defects, counterexamples or already-required behaviour alone is not authorship. Adopted wording, design or policy, including particular repair directions, is authorship of that contribution; calling it a finding does not restore independence. Finding a defect grants no review authority. Reading the same governing sources is allowed, but a fresh context grants neither independence nor authority; self-review remains construction output. Received contributions retain their author's identity wherever carried, and that author's reading is not independent acceptance. Independence across actor families must be declared; absent a stated policy, two activations of one model family are not independent for semantic judgment.
exceptions: A reporter may assess a later repair only when its existing assessment grant, authorship relation and evidence independence permit.
Same-model-family activations count as independent only if the claim's governing basis declares that policy.

grounding.quote:
it does not apply one. A finding
without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

constraints.statement: Return one core result and required evidence record for each actually evaluated declared predicate. Explicitly name planned unperformed predicates without assigning any core value, including indeterminate or falsified. Recommendations are evidence, never applied dispositions. A finding lacking consumer-traceable evidence is commentary.
conditions: A review is returned.
exceptions: A review may recommend a disposition as evidence only.

grounding.quote: | invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

constraints.statement: The projection is total over core values, not over unperformed predicates: those have neither result nor triage. satisfied: explicit no-finding, triage not_applicable, evidence/residuals/invalidation retained; priority/boundary effect not_applicable unless another exact result supplies a finding. falsified: one or more exact findings, triage complete where supported and indeterminate fields where not; apply Product priority/boundary policy without mechanical severity-to-disposition mapping. indeterminate: partial finding/observation, indeterminate triage and exact gaps/residuals; preserve uncertainty or reactivate capable evaluation, never consume as satisfaction or closed finding. out_of_frame: undeclared material relation or missing evaluator capability, indeterminate triage with exact reconfiguration pressure; refine/reconfigure and keep unresolved, never consume as satisfaction or falsification. invalid_basis: basis failure, not_applicable triage, invalidation evidence and repair pressure; refuse consumption and use declared basis re-entry.
constraints.uncertainty: These are descriptions of source-defined results, not results returned by this interpretation.
conditions: A finding-level triage projection is made.
exceptions: For satisfied, another exact consumed result may separately supply a finding affecting priority or boundary effect.

grounding.quote:
The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation

constraints.statement: Every configuration keeps severity, priority, boundary effect and disposition distinct even when Product policy maps values. A recommended disposition is evidence, not priority/boundary effect/disposition, and is never adopted mechanically. Profiles declare fields; Products bind scales. An adjacent out-of-claim observation returns separately with claim-relative triage not_applicable and exact repricing/re-entry pressure; the decision owner routes it to its declared owner without a claim-relative block or new review round from severity alone. The assessor returns to the decision owner, not constructor, and neither edits, directs repair nor authorises continuation. The rule applies to any assessor/owner; EXECUTIVE_BASELINE is an instance binding.

grounding.quote:
for acceptance, a change a proxy cannot make re-enters at its owning
relation

constraints.statement: Acceptance must be the owner's disposition over the unchanged subject and cannot be widened by recording it; it exhausts only its named instance and interval. Review approval, green labels, document/review counts and historical outcomes are not acceptance or work-item closure. A human may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy; proxy identity remains distinct, grant contents belong to IDENTITY §6, absolute proxy limits to FOUNDATIONS §2, and changes beyond the proxy grant re-enter at their owning relation.
constraints.uncertainty: The full proxy-grant tuple and absolute limits are not supplied.
exceptions: A human decision may be exercised by an explicitly admitted bounded proxy.

grounding.quote:
A claim whose disposition is
unresolved cannot be qualified and so cannot be accepted; how the record
is evaluated is [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015).
An intentionally removed disposition is a decision of the current Product
authority, and its record is that decision

constraints.statement: Include the successor disposition record naming the exact immutable predecessor cut and one semantic disposition for every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor. Unresolved claim dispositions cannot be qualified or accepted. Intentional removal is a current Product-authority decision recorded as such; RELEASE §9 owns record evaluation.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete disposition vocabulary and evaluation procedure are not supplied.
conditions: The accepted subject is a successor.

grounding.quote: | a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |

Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff

constraints.statement: A finding can block only if it falsifies the claim, exposes competing/ambiguous acceptance-path authority, violates applicable active authority/safety/retained accepted behaviour, or establishes durable material architectural foreclosure of an admitted Product outcome. These are necessary, not all automatically sufficient. Valid falsification of a mandatory claim under a non-waivable hard stop blocks regardless of priority/cutoff. Otherwise the decision owner decides using exact affected claim, governed outcome/decision, hard stops and Product cutoff policy; below cutoff no automatic block follows and accepted residuals stay explicit. Findings meeting none do not block. Outside observations alone neither widen subject, block the bounded claim nor require another ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment. Severity mechanically selects neither priority nor blocking; priority erases neither severity nor hard stops. This member sets no cutoff.
constraints.uncertainty: Product cutoff and particular hard stops are not instantiated.
conditions: At any promotion boundary a finding is consumed against the exact reviewed claim and applicable hard stops.

grounding.quote:
An analogy or matching result
is insufficient. Evidence for one claim is not reported as a result for
another

constraints.statement: A weak Σ admitting materially different behaviour must declare latitude or be repaired before decision-complete design is claimed. No ladder rung implies another; conformance proves neither identical behaviour outside Σ nor equal cost. Semantic conformance uses the governing semantic basis as Σ. For a proposed span 𝒜 → ℐ and 𝒜 → 𝒞_H, keep conformance, semantic and computational equivalence separate. Categorical equivalence must meet all applicable FOUNDATIONS Formal-fragment items and additionally exhibit a quasi-inverse functor with natural isomorphisms from each composite to its identity functor on a stated domain. Analogy, matching output or passing conformance is insufficient for equivalence or preserved structure; evidence for one claim is not another's result.
constraints.uncertainty: The Formal fragment's definitions of categories, functors, 𝒜, ℐ and 𝒞_H are not supplied.
conditions: A conformance or equivalence claim is made.

grounding.quote:
reconstructability requires a correct reconstruction route, not its
execution at every use, grants no restart authority and does not excuse
stale success. The claim determines the reconstruction span; a local
selected function does not require recreating the whole subject.

A construction outside the declared competence or
configuration envelope cannot indict generic method sufficiency

constraints.statement: Failure to derive a conformant next layer indicates an upper-layer defect: unclear, contradictory, underspecified, insufficiently concrete/decomposable, or polluted with accidental lower-layer detail. Producing an artifact while hiding major unresolved ambiguity is insufficient. Reconstruction scope follows the claim, grants no restart authority and excuses no stale success; new material counterexamples challenge affected relations. After freeze compare to the mandatory governing semantic basis. Lawful alternatives permitted by that basis pass; subjective similarity is insufficient. Byte/structural identity, unique derivation, determinism and incumbent equality are not generic comparison criteria. Out-of-envelope constructions cannot indict generic method sufficiency.
constraints.uncertainty: No competence envelope, frozen construction or reconstruction is evaluated here.
conditions: A layered derivation, reconstruction or frozen-result comparison is assessed.
exceptions: Exact current accepted basis and sufficient evidence may be reused after checking applicability and invalidation.
An applicable separately held reference outcome is optional non-authoritative evidence; equivalence to it is required only when the governing basis requires it.

grounding.quote:
Relocation reported as reduction, or
conservation claimed from unchanged bytes, misreports the claim (§1, P1,
P6). The three heads stay separate in the return as the rungs of the
ladder do above; a frame for a reconstruction task binds this
distinction.

constraints.statement: State each of semantic conservation, demonstrated reduction and mere relocation under separate heads with its own claim and evidence; claim none by byte or size measure. Read both texts against RELEASE §9 dispositions for conservation; trace the same deciding path in both versions under a declared cost measure and tradeoffs for reduction. Relocation without a traced path change is not reduction, and unchanged bytes do not establish conservation. Reconstruction task frames bind this separation.
constraints.uncertainty: RELEASE §9's complete conservation reading is external.
conditions: Returning a task that builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor.

grounding.quote:
A component may
lawfully hold several roles. Three cases are distinguished: behaviour
already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are
each design changes, and only those two require re-entry.

allowed: One component may lawfully hold multiple declared roles.
Behaviour already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation without design re-entry.
forbidden: Treating a new operational responsibility or new semantic/authoritative role as ordinary variation.
Inferring semantic truth or authority from technological capability or out-of-role use.

grounding.quote:
Isolation, substrate, performance, security and
dependency ownership are each lawful grounds for an independent
implementation. The invariant is not that equivalent code is never
rebuilt; it is that a local realisation does not present an existing
accepted semantic or authoritative relation as newly owned local truth

allowed: Independent implementation for isolation, substrate, performance, security or dependency ownership.
Consume, local implementation, optimisation, adaptation or deliberate duplication with stated non-semantic constraints and a semantic disposition.
forbidden: Presenting an existing accepted semantic or authoritative relation as newly owned local truth.
Commonising superficial similarity despite materially non-equivalent governing laws.

grounding.quote:
A worker may be told where to inspect and what
contract to satisfy. A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour

allowed: Tell a worker where to inspect and which contract to satisfy.
forbidden: Using a design-law-enforcement clause without provenance and proof of its continuing intended effect.

grounding.quote:
Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule
